months.name: February
months.objective: Turn Valentine’s-season traffic into first memberships through a mystery-class intro; recruit through members’ love letters; move February renewals onto 3–12 month plans; let lapsed clients come back on the commitment they choose. Every reward is tied to a purchase or a visit.
months.strategy:
Red Flags, Green Flags.

Commercial job: Turn Valentine’s-season traffic into first memberships through a mystery-class intro; recruit through members’ love letters; move February renewals onto 3–12 month plans; let lapsed clients come back on the commitment they choose. Every reward is tied to a purchase or a visit.

Newcomer: Blind Date (No Catfishing) (“Two classes. You don’t know which. That’s the fun part.”). Kenkere’s VDAY50! code (38 uses, ₹2.6L given away at 50%) bought February volume at a huge cost. A booked second visit lifts trial→member from 10.8% to 43.9%, and a mystery format gets newcomers into the class they would never pick, which is usually the one that sells the membership.

Referral: Love Bombing (The Healthy Kind) (“Love bombing, but it’s two free classes and zero manipulation.”). Referrals convert 41.2% at Kwality, 22.6% at Bandra, 28.3% at Kenkere and 76.1% at pop-ups, versus 3.8–5.7% for website leads. The 2026 BOGO codes (70 uses, ₹3.1L given) went mostly to existing clients; this one pays out only when a genuinely new person buys.

Renewal: Put a Ring On It (“If you like it, then you should’ve put a 6-month on it.”). Members using 75%+ of their sessions renew at 82–88%, and longer plans keep them using them. The best perks sit on the longest plans; nothing is unlocked by a class count, so every renewer qualifies.

Lapsed: It’s Not You, It’s Your Schedule (“It’s not you, it’s your schedule. Pick a relationship status.”). Lapsers average 2.6–3.4 visits in the first half of a membership vs 6.4 for renewers: they left because the plan did not fit the week, not because of the price. Letting them pick the commitment removes the objection without deepening the discount.
months.notes: Build: 55 new buyers × ₹11,150 first-60-day spend = ₹6.2L; 60 renewals × ₹23,384 = ₹14.1L; 27 winbacks = ₹3.1L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹2.3L. months.strategy:
Cloud Nine — 9 Years of Physique 57.

Commercial job: Flagship month: win on excitement and economics. Two products that exist only in April (the 9-Month Lease and the 9-Class Pack), a 9:09 flash, a wheel you can double, numbered Club Nine annuals and a month of events, with no offer above 25% effective (cash ≤20% except annuals, the flash and the bulk pack). Every April buyer leaves with a reason to come back in May.

Upgrade: Moving In Together (The 9-Month Lease) (“Nine years in, we’re ready to move in together. 99 keys. No second batch.”). A numbered, one-month-only product gives people a reason to buy now without cutting the price of the core memberships. April 2026 was bought with 40–48% codes; scarcity sells the long plan at 17.5–20% instead.

Renewal: Club Nine: The Founders’ Table (“Nine numbered seats per studio. Founder perks for a year.”). Annual buyers are the most valuable members in the book; a numbered seat with doubled perks costs less than a deeper price and gives them something to show off.

Renewal: Spin Class (Literally) (“Renew, then spin. Every spin wins. Feeling brave? Double it.”). Clients who use 75%+ of their sessions renew at 80–86%. The doubling option pays the prize only when the member books the classes that make them renew again; the expected value of a spin is ≈₹1,900 Mumbai / ₹1,350 Bengaluru.

Newcomer: Party Crasher Pass (“It’s our 9th birthday and you’re invited. 3 classes for ₹999.”). A booked sequence of classes is what converts; the party class gives newcomers the best room of the year, and the buzzer turns a sale into a show for whoever is waiting.

Lapsed: Faking Your Own Death Didn’t Work (“We wrote your obituary. You’re not getting out of it that easily.”). Lapsed clients already know the product; what they need is a moment and a reason that is not just a discount. A personal postcard with a dated class beats a generic reminder.

Referral: Plus One, Plus Nine (“Bring a friend, get 9 days. Bring three, get a month.”). Referrals convert at 22–76% against 3.8–5.7% for website leads. A tier at three friends gives the super-connectors a reason to keep going.

Spot: The 9:09 Panic Attack (“Plank for your price. Or wait for 9:09 and panic with everyone else.”). A price you earn with your body is the most Physique 57 thing there is, and every plank at the desk is a show for whoever is waiting. The floor price (23.7% / 24.0%) sits inside the 25% spot cap, and plan revenue is counted at the floor.

Upgrade: The Cloud Nine 90 (“Ninety classes. One year. Zero commitment issues.”). The Anniversary Big 85 Flex sold 4 times at Kemps Corner and once at Kenkere House in April 2026; this replaces it at a price inside the bulk cap.

months.strategy:
Home for the Holidays.

Commercial job: Students home from college fill empty off-peak seats; Mother's Day duos; keep April's buyers attending.

Newcomer: Mom Said Get Off the Couch (“Home for the summer and Mom's already said 'do something'?”). Weekday 10–12 and weekend 4–7 pm run 27–41% full; the marginal cost of a seat there is near zero. Students arriving home in May are a predictable, untapped audience.

Newcomer: Group Project (Finally, Everyone Pulls Their Weight) (“Group projects: usually one person does all the work. Not here.”). Bulk purchase is one of the few places 25% is allowed. Groups attend together (higher usage → higher renewal) and bring four new names per sale.

Newcomer: Mom-entum (“She carried you for 9 months. You can carry her to class.”). Duos with a booked second class convert best; Mother's Day gives a reason. The perk is a shared session, not a bigger discount.

Renewal: Don't Ghost Us After the Party (“Great party. Now show up 8 times in May.”). 2026 anniversary-code buyers renewed at only 24.5%. Attendance in the month after purchase is the best predictor of renewal; the reward is earned by it.
months.notes: Build: 62 new buyers × ₹11,150 first-60-day spend = ₹6.9L; 68 renewals × ₹23,384 = ₹15.9L; 30 winbacks = ₹3.5L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹2.6L. Renewal: Black Friday Blind Box (No Duds) (“Black Friday, but every box is a winner. We checked.”). Black Friday discounts train members to wait. A mystery bonus keeps the cash discount at the standard ladder (10/15/20%) and makes opening the box the content.

months.strategy:
Party Season Survival Guide.

Commercial job: Renew December’s book onto long plans with perks spread across Q1; sell January starts now with Resolution Insurance; turn gifting into January newcomers; bank pack demand on Boxing Day; win back long-lapsed clients with a plus-one to the NYE Countdown Class.

Renewal: The Advent-ure Calendar (Opens in January) (“An advent calendar you open in January, when you actually need it.”). January drop-off is when renewals are lost. Spreading the perks across Jan–Mar gives members a reason to show up every week of the hardest quarter, which is what keeps them renewing.

Spot: Boxing Day (Gloves Optional) (“Boxing Day. No gloves, just a 12-class pack at 20% off.”). The week after Christmas is empty in studio but busy on phones. A two-day pack price pulls January purchases forward without touching membership prices.

Newcomer: Resolution Insurance (Claim Approved) (“Insure your resolution before you make it. Claim approved.”). Most January resolutions fail in week two. Cover for the usual excuses (late cancels, a bad week) costs little and is exactly what a nervous December buyer needs to hear.

Newcomer: The Gift They Won’t Regift (“The one gift that doesn’t end up in next year’s Secret Santa.”). A gift arrives with a friend’s endorsement, which is why gifted and referred clients convert far better than ad leads. The credit only pays out when the recipient buys.

Lapsed: The Ex-Files: Season Finale (“Every great series needs a finale. Yours is a comeback.”). People who come back in December arrive in January already in the habit. The plus-one turns a returner into a referral at the busiest social week of the year.
months.notes: Build: 75 new buyers × ₹11,150 first-60-day spend = ₹8.4L; 82 renewals × ₹23,384 = ₹19.2L; 37 winbacks = ₹4.2L; privates/retail/drop-ins ₹3.1L.
